title: Record browser events once in Google while preserving the first-party ledger

source.ref: Owner-directed completion of accurate Frequency analytics; root-approved measurement audit followup after LIVE-2275 consent restoration.

detail:
Actual eligible browser event delivery previously called Google once through gtag and again through the authenticated collector and server tracker, producing two same-name provider events and a second profile-based provider identity for one first-party row. The collector now supplies an internal mirrorGa:false option after its unchanged client-event, actual-account and consent gates. The server tracker still records the first-party row and honors durable-key deduplication, then returns before Google for that explicit option; direct authoritative signup, lead and purchase callers retain their existing defaults. The flag is never taken from the untrusted payload, and an unavailable or deployment-disabled browser tag does not trigger a replacement server identity. Actual-module tests execute the browser helper, real collector, taxonomy, request policy, ledger recorder and Google transport with only external auth/database/provider fixtures. On the unchanged LIVE-2275 privacy base93ec5c1 the frozen new consequence test has seven failures and ten passes; after the bounded implementation all17 pass. Exactly one existing collector expected-call tuple is strengthened with the fourth internal false option, as expressly approved by root under the owner instruction to bypass handoff approval checkpoints; every consent, denial and response assertion remains unchanged. The new test and probe bytes are identical before and after the fix. Initial standard pageviews and manual SPA behavior are untouched: the existing first-mount skip works, and read-only Admin evidence confirms the current property has enhanced page/history measurement disabled. No provider settings, live Google events, SQL, reward accounting or advertising-sensitive data are changed. This row proves source delivery consequences, not live Google configuration or deployment acceptance. Focused verification passes157 tests across12 files and lint on five changed code/probe files. Independent privacy peer re-ran48 tests acrossthree files and passed; root reviewed the actual production delta as the third pass. Required backlog passes2697 entries with1004 agreeing probes. Provider settings and live acceptance remain outside this source proof.

2026-11-15 UTC production receipt: external PR #4973 merged as 766068a3961e5b69a61d4ebbda4a138e47a059cc. Vercel production deployment CSXxTZtYqTUSS5UL2HKf2iunjTw2 reached READY; the public /api/status returned HTTP200 with that exact commit, main ref and production environment. The merged tree 778f9d61066e8bdb1ba7e8908c22a7efd4e92b8d is identical to the independently verified virtual merge (67 tests across six files), preserving all seven approved file hashes and the unchanged consequence probe. Actual Chromium anonymous acceptance passed three cases: declined and required-undecided states emitted no Google initialization, and a locally granted consent bootstrap initialized once before fresh withdrawal disabled the flags. Off-origin and non-GET requests were aborted and service workers blocked; no synthetic Google event, provider hit or tracking write was generated. This verifies serving identity and anonymous consent behavior, not live authenticated single-provider-hit delivery, which still needs natural-traffic observation.
